conviction_note: Nothing company-level and unpriced was found: the only GMV read (Jefferies third-party data, Cantor) is sell-side and on the wire, the revenue bar ($3.74B) sits just under the company's own ~$3.76B figure, and two counterparty proxies (PayPal branded checkout +1% with EU de minimis drag; Amazon Prime Day shifted out of Q3) lean slightly the other way, so findings net to -0.4 while p_up sits at 51 on a large abs move; the stock trades on the Q4/BFCM guide, which nobody has sourced, and has sold three of its last five beats.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue consensus $3.74B (Benzinga / Fiscal.ai via Stocktwits 2026-10-15; Hudson Labs $3,742M, 2026-10-07: two agreeing sources) against company guide of low-thirties % growth on Q3 2025 revenue of ~$2.84B, which the 2026-10-26 Finviz preview puts at roughly $3.76B; gross profit guide mid-to-high-twenties % growth; opex 33-34% of revenue; FCF margin high teens to low 20s. Non-GAAP EPS consensus $0.45-0.46, whisper $0.48. Sources: https://finviz.com/news/408250/shopifys-q3-test-can-revenue-beat-its-own-upgraded-guide-as-ai-costs-climb , https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/shopify-q3-2026-earnings-preview-shop-results-preview , https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/Markets/Equity/shop-stock-heads-for-4th-green-week-analysts-see-up-to-10-upside-for-shopify-ahead-of-earnings/cZxWF8LRBAi . No sourced bar for the Q4 guide (Benzinga lists Q4 revenue consensus $4.74B, Hudson Labs $4,750M, but the Q4 guide is the unknown).
positioning_check: Short interest 20.78M shares, 2.6 days to cover as of 2026-10-15 settlement (massive.com, https://massive.com/quote/SHOP); about 1.5-2% of float, not crowded. Earlier: 20.1M / 2.3 days 2026-07-31, 15.4M / 1.1 days 2026-08-14 (curvedtrading, FINRA-sourced). Baseline: 25-delta skew +12.23 vol points (puts rich, 'downside paid'), put/call OI 0.91, event-implied move 12.57%, run-up -4.5% over 5 days and +0.31% over 20, 10.4% off the 52-week high. Stocktwits retail sentiment 'neutral' (2026-10-15).

findings.finding: Jefferies (Buy, $175) said its review of third-party data indicates Q3 GMV could exceed expectations, and Cantor Fitzgerald (Neutral, PT raised to $158 from $145) expects a beat on Q3 GMV, revenue and operating profit with revenue growth in the low 30s; the market bar is $3.74B revenue, just below the company's own ~$3.76B figure.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Shopify beat revenue consensus in each of the last four quarters by about 2-4%, yet the stock fell -6.94% (2025-11-04), -6.70% (2026-02-11) and -15.62% (2026-05-05) on beats; the two big up moves (+21.97% 2025-08-06, +16.98% 2026-08-05) came with an accelerating guide. So the reported-quarter beat alone has not paid.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced. These are wire-carried sell-side notes, and consensus has already moved to $3.74B from $3.57B. If the market had fully taken in a large GMV beat, the skew would not be 12 vol points put-rich and the stock would not be down 4.5% in the five days into the print. What is left is the size of the beat over a consensus that sits under the guide.
findings.independence: The Hudson Labs memo (https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/shopify-q3-2026-earnings-preview-shop-results-preview, 2026-10-07) cites Q2 momentum (GMV +32%, international +37%, payments penetration 68%), but that is backward-looking. No independent card-spend data for Q3 2026 was found.

findings.finding: The Q3 revenue bar ($3.74B consensus) sits just under management's own figure of roughly $3.76B (low-thirties growth on $2.84B), and Shopify has beaten revenue consensus by 2-4% in each of the last four quarters, so on its own record the print is likely about $3.80-3.85B, roughly a 1.5-3% beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same as above: four straight revenue beats produced three declines of 6.7-15.6% and one +17% (on the guide).
findings.why_not_priced: A habitual beat of a bar set below the guide is the expected outcome; the whisper ($0.48 against $0.45 EPS) shows the buy side already expects it. This finding lands inside what the company guided and is sized near zero for that reason.
findings.independence: Partly shares the beat thesis with the Jefferies/Cantor finding but rests on a different basis (the company guide and the beat track record, not third-party GMV data). Track record also from https://www.benzinga.com/quote/SHOP/earnings-forecasts .

findings.finding: PayPal's Q3 2026 release (2026-10-27) showed branded checkout TPV up only about 1% FX-neutral, the fourth straight quarter at 1-2%, with the removal of the EU de minimis exemption cutting about 70bp from branded checkout and tariff pressure in Europe named. That is a counterparty read on cross-border and European online checkout in the same quarter, where Shopify's international GMV grew 37% in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No record of Shopify reacting to a PayPal print; Shopify's international GMV line has not been the cause of a move in the baseline history.
findings.why_not_priced: PayPal spoke after Shopify last did (2026-08-05), and Shopify previews do not cite it. But PayPal's branded checkout has lagged e-commerce for four quarters, so it is a weak proxy. If the market read it as a Shopify negative, previews would flag European or cross-border risk; Hudson Labs only lists tariffs and FX generically.
findings.independence: Proxy only. Shopify has not confirmed any de minimis drag. Global-e (cross-border, Shopify partner) guided Q3 GMV $1.995-2.045B after +44% in Q2 (https://www.taiwannews.com.tw/en/news/6419941, 2026-08-12), which points the other way, but it has not reported Q3.

findings.finding: Amazon's Q3 2026 release said Prime Day moved into Q2 in most large markets this year and that Q3 growth would have been about 400bp higher without the shift (North America +6%). Shopify's Q3 2025 comparison included the July 2025 Prime Day period, when competing promotions run across the web, and Shopify's own Q2 2026 (+34%) may have taken that halo instead, which would make the Q3 comparison tougher.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance in the baseline history; Shopify's Q2 2026 print (+16.98%) came in the quarter that held the shifted Prime Day.
findings.why_not_priced: None of the Shopify previews found mention the Prime Day calendar shift. If the market had priced a timing headwind, the revenue consensus would have been set below the guide for that reason; it sits just below the guide, which fits ordinary conservatism instead.
findings.independence: Inference from a peer's calendar; Shopify has not commented. Hudson Labs flags a 'tough YoY comparison' generically (Q3 2025 GMV $92B, +32%).

findings.finding: Gross-profit quality: Shopify guided Q3 gross-profit growth in the mid-to-high twenties against low-thirties revenue growth; subscription gross margin is just below 80% on Sidekick AI costs, and transaction and loan losses reached 3.9% of revenue as the capital business grew. Margin quality, not revenue, is the named debate.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-05-05 print (-15.62%) beat on revenue and was sold; the margin and opex mix was part of the debate around it, per post-print coverage (https://www.tikr.com/blog/shopify-stock-has-fallen-33-in-2026-could-this-be-the-turning-point).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it is the company's own guide and appears in every preview. The residual is whether loss rates or AI cost step up beyond the guide, which no source quantifies.
findings.independence: Hudson Labs (2026-10-07) lists AI/LLM cost pressure as the top risk; same underlying company disclosure, so it is counted once.
